items.title: 70399_Theodore _Red_ Saunders oral history interview
items.q: you heard with the clarinet on top, you knew that was Glenn Miller

ctx.x: Right, right, right, because you got the full benefit of him, and you got -- and, well, Ellington, and then -- well, you had so many bands. But all of the bands were rhythmetic. Jimmy Lunceford, there's a great band.

So they were rhythmetic, everything -- and they had everything the rest of them had, had the vocals, they had the quartets, they had the whole deal going. And they had that style. And, see, the thing about bands and things then, you could hear a band and you knew who that band was. They had identity, right, so you heard with the clarinet on top, you knew that was Glenn Miller, and you knew Tommy Dorsey's sound, you know Duke Ellington's sound. And so they worked on it to an extent. But then when they started…
